Looking at these numbers, the pattern of early divergence with low edit distance plus a jump in added refusals and curt replies looks more consistent with a system-prompt-level shift than a fine-tune bias, since fine-tuning tends to show later divergence with higher edit distance.

Median 1 suggests the first token often stays the same before diverging, which fits refusal openings like "I" branching differently. Weighing the options, system-prompt bias doesn't match since there's no chattiness or stage directions, while fine-tune bias fits best given the added refusals, curt replies, and dropped disclaimers — so I'll go with fine-tune bias, though with moderate confidence around 0.6 since the effect seems stronger than typical.
